It may have to do with zoning and/or property value of the homes around the little free library. If its an issue with the former, then that's because the little free library is offering a service in the middle of a neighborhood. Businesses are often separated into their own "neighborhoods" (strip-malls or clusters) away from homes, because it generates traffic. A reasonable person in urban housing would most likely wish that the traffic on their street is restricted only to residents and guests, not to attract visitors from outside the neighborhood who wish to peruse in the free service provided.

As for property values, as mentioned before, the free little library would alter the activity of the neighborhood, which may negatively impact the sale of a house around the free little library. Why? Because the traffic caused may induce obstruction or delays in entering or leaving the residence that you pay for. When no-one wants to buy into a home, the property value goes down.

This is all my speculation though.
